$comment: Risk-based suggestions (spec §2.3), as data. A risk fires when its `condition` holds, every clause listed in `absent` is missing from the assembled package, and every clause listed in `present` is in it. Each risk declares the `packages` it applies to, so an employment risk cannot surface inside a commercial contract set. Bodies support the same {{field}} and [[glossary]] tokens as clause bodies. A risk whose `absent` clause is always auto-inserted can never fire; validate.mjs reports those as UNREACHABLE_RISK rather than letting them sit in the corpus as dead content.

risks.title: Missing governing law clause
risks.body: No governing law provision is present. Add one naming {{formStateLong}} to match the state of formation. Without it, which state's law applies is decided by a judge applying conflict-of-laws rules.

risks.title: Entity structure conflicts with funding plan
risks.body: You selected VC funding but an LLC. Institutional funds generally cannot hold LLC interests because pass-through income creates UBTI for their tax-exempt LPs. Nearly every priced round requires a Delaware C-Corp, and converting later triggers legal and tax cost you can avoid by forming as a C-Corp now.

risks.title: Employee non-competes are void in California
risks.body: California voids employee non-competes, and it is unlawful to include or attempt to enforce one — regardless of where the agreement was signed or which state's law it names. Employers were also required to notify current and former employees whose agreements contained one. Rely on confidentiality and invention assignment instead.

risks.title: Out-of-state choice of law will not hold for California employees
risks.body: The Company is organized in {{formStateLong}} but employs in California. A provision requiring a California employee to litigate outside California or under another state's law is voidable at the employee's election, and an employee who voids it recovers attorney's fees. The exception is narrow: it applies only where the employee was individually represented by counsel in negotiating that term.

risks.title: Contractor engagement likely fails California's ABC test
risks.body: California presumes employment. Prong B requires the work to sit outside the Company's usual course of business, and the Company's business is {{industryName}} — so engaging a contractor to do that same work is unlikely to qualify no matter how the agreement is written. Exposure on reclassification includes unpaid overtime, meal and rest premiums, business expenses, payroll taxes, and penalties, and can reach individuals personally.

risks.title: Five-employee threshold turns on several obligations at once
risks.body: At {{headcountBand}}, California turns on FEHA discrimination and harassment law, CFRA family leave, pregnancy disability leave, mandatory harassment prevention training, the Fair Chance Act, bereavement and reproductive loss leave, and off-duty cannabis protections. These attach the moment headcount crosses five and count part-time and temporary workers.

risks.title: Workplace Violence Prevention Plan required
risks.body: At {{headcountBand}} the Company needs a written workplace violence prevention plan separate from its safety program, plus annual training and a violent incident log retained for five years. This is a distinct Cal/OSHA citation from the injury and illness program.

risks.title: An LLC cannot render licensed services in California
risks.body: California does not permit a limited liability company to provide professional services requiring a licence. This is a formation-blocking issue rather than a drafting preference — the correct vehicle is a professional corporation or a registered limited liability partnership, with ownership restricted to licensees. For medical services the corporate practice doctrine restricts ownership further.

risks.title: California corporate law may apply despite out-of-state incorporation
risks.body: Incorporating in {{formStateLong}} does not by itself escape California corporate law. Where more than half of property, payroll, and sales are in California and more than half of voting shares are held by California residents, California rules govern cumulative voting, director removal, distributions, dissenters' rights, indemnification limits, and inspection rights. Test this annually — the answer changes as the company grows.

risks.title: California annual tax accrues on doing business here
risks.body: California charges {{caAnnualTax}} for doing business in the state, whether or not the Company was formed here and whether or not it made money. An LLC additionally owes {{caLlcFeeTiers}} — computed on gross California income, so a low-margin business can owe it while operating at a loss. The liability continues until the entity is formally dissolved.

risks.title: California final pay timing carries a per-day penalty
risks.body: A terminated employee must be paid all wages, including accrued vacation, at the time of termination. An employee who resigns with 72 hours' notice must be paid on their last day; without notice, within 72 hours. Late final pay accrues a waiting time penalty of one full day of wages per day late, up to thirty days — a payroll timing error alone can cost a month of wages per employee.

risks.title: Use-it-or-lose-it vacation policies are unenforceable in California
risks.body: Accrued vacation is wages in California and cannot be forfeited. Accrual may be capped at a reasonable multiple of the annual rate, but a policy that zeroes a balance at year end is void and produces a wage claim at every departure. An unlimited-PTO policy avoids accrual only if administered so employees actually take leave.

risks.title: Meal and rest premiums are the most common California wage claim
risks.body: Each missed, late, or interrupted meal period and each missed rest period entitles a non-exempt employee to one additional hour of pay at the regular rate — separately, so a single bad day can owe two hours. The premium is measured at the regular rate including non-discretionary bonuses, not base pay, and unpaid premiums cascade into wage statement and waiting time claims.

risks.title: California automatic renewal law applies to this contract
risks.body: The term auto-renews and California regulates that directly: renewal terms must be clear and conspicuous in visual proximity to acceptance, consent must be affirmative and separate, a post-transaction acknowledgment is required, and cancellation must be as easy as signup and available in the same medium. Goods delivered under a non-compliant renewal may be treated as an unconditional gift, and the statute carries a private right of action.

risks.title: Employee and applicant data is now consumer data in California
risks.body: The HR data exemption expired. Applicants, employees, and contractors are consumers with rights to know, delete, correct, and limit use of sensitive information about their own employment data. A notice at collection is required, and any employee monitoring — device, location, or communications — has to appear in it.

risks.title: No local ordinance selected — confirm that is right
risks.body: No California city ordinance layer is applied to this package. Dozens of California cities and counties set minimum wage, paid sick leave, and fair scheduling rules above the state floor, and coverage follows where the employee physically works — including a remote employee's home city. Confirm the work location against the local ordinance list rather than assuming state law is the whole picture.

risks.title: 83(b) election has a hard 30-day deadline
risks.body: The election must be postmarked within 30 days of the grant — {{d83bDeadline}} for this package. Late filing cannot be cured, and the consequence is ordinary income tax on the spread as each tranche vests.

risks.title: HIPAA business associate coverage missing
risks.body: Healthcare business with no Business Associate Agreement obligation in the package. Disclosing PHI to a vendor without a BAA is itself a HIPAA violation, independent of any breach.

risks.title: New York publication deadline running
risks.body: Publication in two designated newspapers and a Certificate of Publication are due within 120 days — {{nyDeadline}}. The run takes six weeks, so starting late makes the deadline impossible. Missing it suspends the LLC's authority to do business in New York until cured.

risks.title: Operating outside the state of formation
risks.body: Formed in {{formStateLong}}, operating in {{opStateLong}}. Transacting business without qualifying there typically means back fees and penalties, and closes that state's courts to you until you register.

risks.title: Delaware franchise tax accrues from day one
risks.body: Delaware charges franchise tax and requires an annual report regardless of revenue. Corporations using the authorized-shares method are often surprised by the first bill; the assumed-par-value method is usually far cheaper and is elected on the same form.

risks.title: Two owners, no deadlock mechanism
risks.body: An even two-way split with no tiebreak means any single disagreement on a matter requiring approval can freeze the company. Add a buy-sell auction, a casting vote, or a neutral third seat.

risks.title: Single-member LLC formalities
risks.body: Single-member LLCs are the most common target for veil-piercing arguments. Keep a separate bank account, document decisions in writing, and avoid paying personal expenses from the Company account.

risks.title: Lien deadlines are jurisdiction-specific and unforgiving
risks.body: Mechanics lien rights depend on preliminary notices served within a statutory window that varies by state and by role on the project. Calendar them at contract execution, not at the time of a dispute.

risks.title: Release will not reach unknown claims without a Section 1542 waiver
risks.body: Under California law a general release does not extend to claims the releasing party did not know or suspect to exist unless it expressly waives [[Civil Code §1542|section 1542]], quoting the statute. Unknown claims are ordinarily the principal reason a release is taken, so a settlement or termination release drafted without it buys much less than intended.

risks.title: PAGA turns any wage violation into a workforce-wide claim
risks.body: California penalties are assessed per employee per pay period, and a single employee can pursue them on behalf of the whole workforce. A wage statement defect worth a few dollars to one person becomes a company-wide claim. Almost every California obligation in this package is PAGA-enforceable, which is why a documented wage and hour review before any notice arrives is worth far more than the same work done after.

risks.title: Local ordinances apply on top of state law
risks.body: Employees work in {{caCityName}}. {{caCitySummary}} Local rules stack rather than replace, the more employee-favorable provision governs, and coverage follows where the employee physically works — so a single remote hire can pull the Company into an ordinance it has no other connection to.

risks.title: Cal-WARN notice applies to any reduction in force
risks.body: At {{headcountBand}}, sixty days' written notice is required before a mass layoff, relocation, or termination of operations. Cal-WARN reaches further than the federal statute in every direction: lower threshold, part-time employees counted, relocations covered, and no requirement that a whole facility close. Damages are back pay and benefits for each day of shortfall. Plan any reduction against this period from the start rather than discovering it mid-process.

risks.title: Pay differentials need a documented, listed justification
risks.body: California compares substantially similar work across all locations, and a differential must rest on a closed list of factors. Prior salary is not one of them, so pay set by matching a candidate's last salary is difficult to defend. Record the basis for each rate at the time it is set — reconstructing it after a comparator has been identified is much weaker.

risks.title: Website tracking is generating high-volume wiretapping claims
risks.body: California's wiretapping statute is being applied to session recording, chat widgets, and third-party advertising pixels, with statutory damages per violation and no need to show actual harm. Audit what runs on the site, obtain consent through a compliant interface before any of it loads, disclose the vendors, and allocate the risk in the contract rather than leaving it to the general indemnity.

risks.title: Accessibility claims carry statutory damages in California
risks.body: The Unruh Act adds statutory damages per violation and attorney's fees on top of federal accessibility law, and an ADA violation is a per se Unruh violation. California carries a disproportionate share of website accessibility filings. Build customer-facing interfaces to a stated standard and allocate remediation responsibility in the contract.
